questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had dreamed of visiting California, and Los Angeles in particular, for a long time. Being in a city and close to the entertainment industry and being able to take courses in film at UCLA were also motivating factors for me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unfortunately, Covid-19 restrictions played a role in my exchange experience since the first half of my programme was almost entirely online.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: As far as I remember, we received emails from UCLA and UCEAP Reciprocity before and after arrival with instructions. However, there wasn't one single official in-person orientation or event for exchange/international students who had just arrived, which was something I would have liked to have. Some things I had to find out on my own

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Received emails from UCLA and UCEAP Reciprocity

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I joined the facebook group for UCPH students going abroad to the UC campuses – here I spoke to other students who were going to UCLA who recommended the UCHA Co-op right next to the UCLA campus. For the price (around half the price of the on-campus dorms including food) and proximity to campus, as well as social opportunities, I would recommend checking out the Co-op (note in your application that you are a UCEAP Reciprocity/exchange/international student – this can give you a better chance of getting a spot there)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: At the co-op specifically (which is student run), you're only a couple minutes away from campus which is great. The amenities and quality of the rooms isn't the best, but is alright. Do note that most people will have to live in a triple or double room (1-2 roommates) upon arrival but also some single rooms, and after a quarter or two you might be able to move to a room with less roommates if you like

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I applied for the on-campus dorms as well and got an offer for a triple room (two roommates) including food for around DKK 10,000 per month. If you want to save money, the Co-op might be a good option

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UCLA has different enrollment 'passes' on MyUCLA which is determined by factors such as your college year/level or your major – make sure you check the specific requirements for each of the classes you're interested in taking before enrollment starts, and make sure to enroll as soon as possible! Some courses are more popular than others – I was lucky that I got all my desired courses but it's better to be prepared in advance, especially if you're looking at specific courses you really want to enroll in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received emails from UCLA regarding enrollment and enrollment passtimes (when enrollment starts), and you can log onto MyUCLA and explore courses and add them to your 'Class Planner' to visualize how your weekly schedule could look before enrollment starts.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Before arrival, I was hoping to be able to enroll in some practical/studio courses within a particular major. Unfortunately, some majors have restrictions on specific types of classes if you're in another major, which restricted my enrollment. Fortunately, I was able to enroll in all the other courses I was interested in (including lower-level/more theoretical courses within said major)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a list of all courses you're interested in, try to see how they fit into your schedule, make sure you read the requirements/prerequisites on the Schedule of Classes or MyUCLA for each class you're interested in, and make sure to check your emails and your MyUCLA account to see which enrollment passtime you can enroll in – and enroll as soon as enrollment starts to be safe

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was generally very satisfied with my courses – many of the ones I took were quite introductory or lower-level and outside of my major at home, which was a nice opportunity to try different types of courses and subjects. The level of a couple of my courses was not that advanced, but this can differ depending on which level and which major your courses are in.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses with numbers between 20 and around 124 – the lower numbers indicate introductory courses, and the higher numbers indicate mid-level or upper-level courses. Overall, personally, I didn't find the general level to be too difficult, but again, this can depend whether you're taking introductory, upper-division courses or masters' courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Some of my courses consisted of a weekly lecture and no discussion seminars, while another course I took had two lectures a week and one discussion section a week. This section differed from my seminars at UCPH, however, in that it mostly consisted of my TA briefly going over some points from the lectures instead of being based on mainly group discussions and classroom 'activation'. I found it a bit difficult at times not having a combination of lectures and discussions with other students, which also made it a bit more difficult meeting new people in/around class.
Furthermore, I took a practical in-person course which had little theory which was a nice contrast to more theoretical courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Beginning Martial Arts (Dance/Worlds Arts & Cultures major), Evolutionary Psychology (Anthropology), Introduction to American Indian Studies (American Indian Studies), Experimental Film, Digital Cinematography, Film Editing – Overview of History, Technique, and Practice (Film/Television)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Experimental Film was quite fascinating and inspiring. Evolutionary Psychology was very interesting, but also a bit challenging if you haven't taking an introductory course in evolution or aren't a biology/psychology/anthropology major. I'd recommend Introduction to American Indian Studies as well!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Most weekly meals at the Co-op were included in the price of rent – I did buy extra groceries in addition to this but wouldn't strictly be needed most of the time. Extra/unexpected costs would include uber, uber eats, going out, getting film (photos) developed, cultural events such as movie tickets, museums, restaurants... I also went on a roadtrip with some friends which included car rental, meals, and hotels/airbnbs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Many things were around the same price as in Denmark. Some food, movie tickets, public transportation were a bit cheaper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Partly due to Covid-19 restrictions, I ended up not participating in much, as some clubs were closed for the winter quarter

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many! There's a whole page (UCLA Rec) with hundreds of different clubs/activities such as sports, creative clubs, societies etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend signing up for something you're interested in or interested in trying! I signed up for the archery club where I met some nice people – they also arranged meetups and activities outside practice

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See all the tourist sites, the beach, Hollywood, DTLA... There's so much to explore and LA is a huge area. I went to Santa Barbara for the weekend while I was there which was really nice – would also recommend going around California or the neighboring states if possible! There are many beautiful national parks in and around California that are amazing to see in-person. I also enjoyed spending time along the coast, in Santa Monica, Venice, Malibu, and going hiking in the hills.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In general it was pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try signing up for clubs and activities and talk to people in your classes and at your dorm/the co-op (if you live here)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many undergraduate students are a bit younger than UCPH students

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Many opportunities for activities and different events, and people can seem pretty open in general

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Save money (and try to apply for scholarships/legater!) before you go – there are so many things, activities and cool places to visit that you'd want to experience if possible

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at other UCPH students' evalutations on this page, talk to other UCPH students who are planning on going to UC or your specific UC campus, look at which courses each UC campus have and which ones you're especially interested in enrolling in – but do also prioritize which city/place you would like to live in as this can play a big role in which environment you have a chance to explore daily – as well as which type of environment (city, beach town, closer to nature...) you might thrive in and enjoy!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in Los Angeles and explore the city/area, going on a road trip to California and neighboring states and seeing some very different and fascinating places, landscapes, and nature, meeting new people, and becoming more independent

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid-19 restrictions on campus and in my dorm the first half of my programme made it harder to meet new people, which was especially challenging in the beginning where you don't necessarily know anyone upon arrival. Hopefully, this might not be the case after 2022, however! It was also challenging at times trying to balance everything in daily life yourself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you're interested in going on exchange and it's a possibility for you, I very much recommend it! It's really cool getting to live in another country for a longer period of time in contrast to a shorter vacation, and it makes you understand aspects of the local culture(s) and daily life more, puts your life in Denmark into perspective, and provides many social and cultural opportunities and experiences.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
